name: Magasin III
funding: Robert Weil Family Foundation, funded by the Weil family office Proventus.

name: Museum Tinguely
funding: Roche has paid all operating costs since the museum opened in 1996 as a gift for its centenary; Roche built it and funds collection additions.

name: Kunstmuseum Bern
funding: Canton Bern and the Burgergemeinde's museum foundation fund it. UBS is main sponsor. Mobiliar and UNIQA sponsor exhibitions. Eight funding foundations include Hansjörg Wyss's Stiftung GegenwART.

name: Usine Kugler (Fédération des Artistes de Kugler)
Fondation Beyeler
funding: CHF 30M budget. Basel-Stadt and Riehen give about 9%; the Beyeler Foundation covers a 27% deficit. Sponsors include UBS (Artist Talks) and Globus.

name: Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen
funding: 2024 income CHF 684k: Stadt St.Gallen 208k, Kanton 196k, other grants 165k (Swisslos, Pro Helvetia, foundations), members and Club der 20 CHF 105k, with UBS and Julius Bär listed.

name: Fotomuseum Winterthur
funding: City of Winterthur gives CHF 738k a year for 2025-2032; also Canton of Zurich, Verein, Volkart Stiftung, Ringier, Monterosa and about 20 foundations.

name: Migros Museum
funding: Institution of the Migros-Kulturprozent, carried by the Migros cooperative federation, which pays a turnover-based sum into culture since 1957. The sheet lists CHF 12 tickets and no public funder.

name: Tishreen War Panorama (October War Panorama)
funding: Run by the Syrian Ministry of Defence, which lists it among its army museums. North Korea helped build it, per Wikipedia and Public Delivery.

name: MOCA Taipei
funding: Its support page lists the sponsors Thermos, Contemporary Art Foundation, Sony, Epson and Royal Inn.

name: Taipei Contemporary Art Center
funding: Artist-run space founded 2010. In 2013 its director said most money came from sales of donated artworks, plus a small government subsidy (about 15%).

name: Dar Foto Festival
funding: Founded by Andrew Munuwa with Valentin Rudloff.
